faculty.department: Department of Computer Science (DIKU), Machine Learning Section
faculty.lab: SAINTS Lab (saintslab.github.io) - Sustainable AI, Neural, and Trustworthy Systems
faculty.research_areas: Efficient ML, ML for sciences, medical image analysis, graph neural networks, sustainability/environmental impact of AI (author of the book 'Sustainable AI', 2025), data frugality and hyper-datafication in frontier AI.
faculty.why_match: Akshat's diffusion-pretraining result is fundamentally a data/compute-efficiency question - a frozen DDPM encoder retains >80% of fine-tuned liver segmentation performance while needing zero labelled fine-tuning epochs, but this benefit does NOT transfer to kidney, an unresolved negative result about when pretraining actually buys efficiency. Selvan's 2026 ICML paper 'Position: Neglecting the Sustainability of AI is fuelling a Global AI Arms Race' (Bakhtiarifard et al., arXiv:2502.20016) and his co-authored 'Efficiency is Not Enough: A Critical Perspective of Environmentally Sustainable AI' (Communications of the ACM 68(7):62-69, 2025, with Christian Igel) argue that efficiency claims in ML need to be interrogated rather than assumed - exactly the discipline Akshat's honest reporting of the kidney failure embodies rather than hiding it. His medical-image-analysis + graph-neural-network thread is also a direct topical match for the segmentation/label-scarcity work (A, C).

faculty.why_match: Akshat's semi-supervised spine-MRI work found that MC-dropout uncertainty and confidence thresholding give comparable pseudo-label filtering quality, and that per-class thresholds calibrated on just 5 reference images match those from 304 - a small-sample calibration-efficiency result. Igel's PAC-Bayesian line, most recently 'Chebyshev-Cantelli PAC-Bayes-Bennett Inequality for the Weighted Majority Vote' (NeurIPS 2021, with Yi-Shan Wu, Andres Masegosa, Stephan Lorenzen, Yevgeny Seldin) and his stated current interest in 'uncertainty quantification in machine learning' is the theoretical machinery that would explain WHY such small-sample calibration can work at all. His ICML 2024 'Smooth Min-Max Monotonic Networks' paper shows he still designs constrained-by-construction architectures - the same design philosophy behind HiME's chain-rule decoding rule (interest D).
